name: HV9961LG-G
title: HV9961: average-current-mode constant-current LED driver controller, 8 V to 450 V
summary: A controller for a low-side buck LED driver that switches an external N-channel MOSFET with a constant off-time and regulates the average current, not the peak, from the switch current alone, so no loop compensation and no high-side sensing are needed and the LED current holds within ±3%. It runs straight from 8 V to 450 V through an internal regulator. The current is set by a 275 mV reference over a sense resistor, or by a 0 V to 1.5 V linear dimming input; a TTL-level PWM input gates the output, and a 0.44 V current-limit comparator gives hiccup short-circuit protection. It is pin-compatible with the HV9910B and can replace it in many designs.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: Low-side buck LED driver. The LED string and the inductor run in series from the input rail down to the MOSFET drain; the diode returns the inductor current to the rail while the switch is off. The HV9961 runs from the same rail through VIN. RCS under the MOSFET source sets the average LED current, RT sets the fixed off-time, and PWMD and LD are tied to VDD so the part runs at full current from the internal 275 mV reference.

operation.text: In a low-side-switch buck converter, the controller averages the MOSFET source current seen at CS and regulates that average in a fast open-loop way, so the LED current does not depend on inductance, switching frequency or output voltage, and the loop needs no compensation. Switching uses a constant off-time; unlike the HV9910B, there is no constant-frequency mode.
RT connects between the RT pin and GND. The HV9910B option of connecting it from RT to GATE is not supported by this part.
Regulation works up to D ≤ 0.75: with the LED string above 75% of VIN, the LED current can fall. With the string below VO(MIN) the current rises instead and can trip the short-circuit protection.

When CS goes above 0.44 V the comparator holds the gate off for THICCUP, 400 µs typical, then retries; this keeps the inductor current from stepping up cycle after cycle into saturation when the output voltage is too low. CS has leading-edge blanking so switching spikes trip neither the current loop nor this comparator.

Below 1.5 V at LD, the 275 mV reference gives way to 0.185 × VLD. The gate stops when VLD drops under 150 mV and runs again once VLD rises over 200 mV; some applications use the same brightness signal to turn the lamp off. A PWM signal under 1.5 V in amplitude on LD gives mixed-mode dimming with a wider dimming ratio.

With 8 VDC to 450 VDC at VIN, VDD is regulated to 7.5 V. Outside circuits may draw from VDD up to the rated maximum current or the package thermal limit, the lower of the two. VDD takes a low-ESR bypass capacitor, which supplies the gate driver's high-frequency current. Alternatively the part runs from a supply applied directly at VDD, above 7.5 V and below 12 V.

Although VIN is rated 450 V instantaneous, the package dissipation limits the continuous voltage. A resistor or a Zener in series with VIN moves part of the loss out of the chip when a higher supply is needed.
Recommended MOSFET gate charge: below 25 nC up to 100 kHz switching, below 15 nC above 100 kHz.

PWMD low stops the gate; high lets it run. Inductor slew limits the current's rise and fall. The first cycle after PWMD goes high ends when CS reaches 275 mV (or 0.185 × VLD), and the current settles within 3 to 4 cycles whatever the switching frequency. The response is close to that of the HV9910B.
Pin-compatible with the HV9910B and usable as a drop-in replacement in many of its designs, without the peak-to-average current error of that part.
